task.title: Reply to a doctor about a delayed, haemolysed sample
task.brief: You are the lab technician on duty. Read the doctor's message and the internal lab notes below. Take about 15 minutes. Write the reply you would send to the doctor (it may be shown to your lab in-charge). A good reply apologises, explains honestly and simply why the result may be wrong, says what you will do now for the patient, and says what the lab will change so it does not happen again. Keep it short, polite and professional. Do not give the patient a diagnosis.
task.material:
WhatsApp message from Dr. Meena Rao (clinic), 10:40 am:

"This is the third time this month. My patient Mr. Arjun S. (58) gave blood at your home collection yesterday at 8 am.
The report came only at 9 pm and shows potassium 6.8. He has no symptoms and his last value was 4.2.
I had to call him at night and worry him. Now he says he does not want to give blood again.
What is going on with your lab? I need an explanation today."

Lab notes (internal): sample reached the lab at 2 pm (bike delayed in traffic, no cool box).
Serum was visibly haemolysed. The report was released without a remark.
key_points: Apologises sincerely for the delay and the worry caused
Explains the sample was delayed and haemolysed, which can falsely raise potassium
Admits the report should have carried a remark or been held
Offers a free, quick recollection (home visit) and a fast repeat report
Suggests the doctor treat the 6.8 value as unreliable until the repeat, without diagnosing
Names fixes: cool box and time limits for home collection, haemolysis check before release
Professional, calm tone; no blaming the patient or the rider

rubric.label: Correct explanation
rubric.guide: 0 = wrong or no reason given, 3 = mentions delay only, 5 = clearly links delay and haemolysis to a falsely high potassium

rubric.label: Action for the patient
rubric.guide: 0 = no next step, 3 = vague offer, 5 = clear free recollection and quick repeat with a time

rubric.label: Prevention
rubric.guide: 0 = nothing, 3 = general promise, 5 = specific changes to transport and report checks

rubric.label: Tone and clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = defensive or rude, 3 = polite but long or unclear, 5 = short, honest, polite and professional
